text: The owner of Osprey-6 is the Prism team, and every change to Osprey-6 goes through their review.
Nadia Underhill is on the pager rotation of Godwit-8 this month, with a deputy as backup. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The language of Godwit-8 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.

Unlike Osprey-6, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Curlew-8 is November 24, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Curlew-8 applies to Osprey-6, the retirement date differs.

Unlike Dunlin-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Osprey-6 is February 1, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Osprey-6 applies to Dunlin-4, the retirement date differs.
Pages from Osprey-6 land on the pager rotation of Oren Fairbanks before anyone else.
Kestrel-2 listens on port 3367; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Dunlin-4 has one owner, the Ledger team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Dunlin-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Kestrel-2 is the Harbor team. Nobody should assume the owner of Kestrel-2 applies to Dunlin-4, the owner differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Curlew-8, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Osprey-6 is Go. Nobody should assume the language of Osprey-6 applies to Curlew-8, the language differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Osprey-6, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Avocet-9 is 2050 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Avocet-9 applies to Osprey-6, the rate limit differs.
Unlike Curlew-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Dunlin-4 is 5967. Nobody should assume the port of Dunlin-4 applies to Curlew-8, the port differs.
Curlew-8 runs in the Osaka datacenter, next to its database.
Source for Kestrel-2 is written in Haskell; no other language is allowed in its repository. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Source for Curlew-8 is written in Zig; no other language is allowed in its repository.

Unlike Dunlin-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Godwit-8 is the Anvil team. Nobody should assume the owner of Godwit-8 applies to Dunlin-4, the owner differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Plan around the retirement date of Dunlin-4: August 15, 2028 is when it goes dark. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The language of Avocet-9 is Haskell, which new contributors must know. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Godwit-8, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Curlew-8 is Lucia Fairbanks. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Curlew-8 applies to Godwit-8, the pager rotation differs.

Unlike Dunlin-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Avocet-9 is the Bergen datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Avocet-9 applies to Dunlin-4, the datacenter differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Avocet-9 at $930k, reviewed every quarter.

Unlike Kestrel-2, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Osprey-6 is 2750 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Osprey-6 applies to Kestrel-2, the rate limit differs.

Unlike Curlew-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Dunlin-4 is the Tallinn datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Dunlin-4 applies to Curlew-8, the datacenter differs.
Dunlin-4 was granted a budget of $2095k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
Godwit-8 runs in the Osaka datacenter, next to its database.
The rate limit of Godwit-8 is 4100 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Dunlin-4, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Curlew-8 is 5945. Nobody should assume the port of Curlew-8 applies to Dunlin-4, the port differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.

Unlike Osprey-6, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Kestrel-2 is 4250 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Kestrel-2 applies to Osprey-6, the rate limit differs.
Pages from Kestrel-2 land on the pager rotation of Nadia Sandoval before anyone else. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Avocet-9 reaches its retirement date on March 16, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
